title: Spark has no emergency response protocol — both the ecosystem-wide and Agent-specific procedures are unwritten
content:
Two sections exist to hold Spark's crisis procedures. `Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response` (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.5) covers "situations that impact the entire Sky Ecosystem." `Agent-Specific Emergency Response` (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.6) covers "situations solely impacting Spark versus the broader Sky Ecosystem." Both contain one sentence of content, and it is the same sentence: "This protocol will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact."

The absence is conspicuous next to what the surrounding sections do specify. Spark has a documented 48-hour deadline for a Delegate's response to a compromised signing key (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.7.3), a 10-day timelock and Guardian veto on its Morpho vault, supply caps in the hundreds of millions, and a seven-day review clock on proposals. The processes governing a delegate's laptop are more fully specified than the processes governing a protocol emergency.

This matters because emergencies are exactly where a governance framework's slow paths fail. Every routine control here runs on multi-day timescales — 7-day review, 10-day timelock, snapshot-block voting windows — and none of them can respond to an exploit in progress. The unwritten sections are precisely the ones that would say who may act inside those windows and on what authority.

In the interim, the only fast-acting powers the Artifact grants anyone are the SRC's immediate Delegate offboarding and the Guardian's veto. Whatever actually happens during a live incident is therefore undocumented and, by the Artifact's own logic, unaccountable — there is no specification to hold an actor to.
description: A.6.1.1.1.3.1.5 and A.6.1.1.1.3.1.6 each contain only a promise that the protocol 'will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact'.
